meta.name: Cuff & Collar
meta.note: A clothes shop. Three shirts, one hat and one pair of sunglasses on the rail each morning, drawn from a rail of ten of each.

text: Linnet. I put the rail out at nine and I take what is left of it in at seven.
Three shirts, a hat and a pair of sunglasses. Never the same five twice.

again.text: Rail is where I left it. Have a look.

choices.text: How do I put it on?

wearing.text: Press G and you have your wardrobe. Move with the arrows, E to put a thing on or take it off again. Your old one goes back in the bag — nothing gets lost in here.

text: Ten shirts on the books, ten hats, ten pairs of glasses. Five of them out at a time.
So no, I will not fetch one from the back. Come by in the morning.

after.text: Wear it in good health. I will buy it back off you when you tire of it.

bye.text: Suit yourself. That is rather the idea.

acquaintance: Rail is out. Three shirts, a hat, a pair of glasses, and one of them is a mistake I stand by.
Somebody tried on every hat and bought none. That is allowed. It is not encouraged.
The beret is back on the rail. It goes out, it comes back, it goes out. Nobody wants it and I refuse to notice.
You are wearing it the right way round. That puts you ahead of most of my customers.
friend: You keep buying the same colour. I have started hiding it so you have to look at the others.
Somebody brought back a straw hat with a bite out of it. I bought it. I am not proud.
I dreamed the whole rail was aviators. Woke up and checked. Two. It was fine.
Ten hats on the books, and I have watched you try to work out which nine are in the back. Do not.
close: Go on, look. I put the good one out because I knew you were due.
The rail can wait. Sit on the counter. I know I said not to, and I am saying it now.
Your old shirt is still in the back. I could not sell it. I did not try very hard.
